frequency_question: How often does an emerging market central bank raise rates within 87 days of holding steady?
membership_rule: Members are instances where a major emerging market central bank, having held its benchmark rate flat for at least four consecutive policy meetings, initiates a rate hike cycle within a subsequent 3-month window. Excluded are easing cycles and emergency interventions driven solely by sovereign default.

cases.name: Banco Central do Brasil pivot to hike

provenance_note: 3 cases named, 4 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.3x)
coverage_note: 3 named; believed roughly 4 in total across comparable major emerging market peers in the reference window.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller frontier markets with idiosyncratic capital controls.
skeleton: Three major emerging market central bank tightening cycles initiated after extended holds, yielding 3 hits out of 4 comparable instances.
validity_reason: Central bank reaction functions to inflation and currency stability evolve over multi-year structural horizons rather than months.
